summary: A five-bay timber long hall with two doors, a covered porch, a hanging sign and a chimney at each end of the ridge, parameterised by width, depth, wall height, bay count, roof pitch and seed.
objective: Seen from about fifteen metres the hall reads as three tiers: long ridge with two chimneys and a porch, then a bay rhythm of posts and recessed openings, then pegs, sill drips and worn step nosings.
intent_signals: reusable building module with attachment sockets
example_prompts: Put a long hall at the head of the village green.
I need a wide timber building with a porch and two chimneys.
not_for: Any claim about the joinery or plan of a specific historical hall.

silhouette: 12 m ridge at 5.15 m with a 30 cm eave overhang, unbroken along the whole length
two brick chimneys with stone caps and clay pots breaking the ridge at 6.54 m
monopitch porch standing 1.4 m clear of the front wall on two posts and stone pads
medium: five-bay rhythm: six frame posts per long wall standing 7 cm proud of the plaster, with top plate, sill beam, mid rail and corner braces kept clear of the openings
windows recessed 12 cm behind a 24 cm wall with a 7 cm frame and two glazing bars, cut as real holes
roof laid as lapped tile courses, roughly three per metre of slope, with a barge board at each verge
two plank doors set back in their reveals under timber hoods, each on a projecting stone step
fine: hexagonal peg heads 9 cm across at every frame joint, three per post: sill, mid rail and plate
sill drip groove under each window, a 2.4 cm shadow line below the sill lip
clenched nail heads and strap hinges on the door leaves, 2.4 cm across
one slipped tile per slope and per-course hue jitter of about 4 percent
worn lighter arris along each stone step nosing and along the sill beams

principles: A long building is read by its bay rhythm: repeat one bay honestly and let the seed move the posts, rather than modelling five different bays.
The porch exists to break a 12 m eave line. Without one interruption the silhouette is a shed no matter how good the surface is.
Two chimneys placed off centre say the hall has two hearths and therefore two rooms; one central chimney would say something else.
implementation: Call create({ width, depth, wallHeight, bayCount, roofPitchDeg, seed }); the returned group is centred on its footprint with y = 0 at the ground plane.
Attach chimney pots, banners or a lean-to through the named sockets rather than by hand-placing world coordinates.
bayCount drives the opening count directly, so a wider hall gets more bays rather than wider windows.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
Two instances with different seeds move the frame posts and the chimney positions while keeping the same ridge line.
The door socket lands on the front wall face, on the bay that is not under the porch: its z equals half the depth parameter.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here is a measurement of any real hall, joinery method or material.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters, not a guarantee at every combination; bayCount 8 costs about 13800 triangles.
footprint_m is the nominal plan. The built bounding box is 12.4 x 7.3 m because the eaves, the porch and the door steps all project past it.
Tuned against ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 with no post-processing; a different exposure changes how the fine band reads.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Swap the palette to move the hall between the listed looks, or raise wallHeight and drop roofPitchDeg for a barn rather than a hall.

defaults.rationale: Five bays over 12 m give a 2.3 m bay, wide enough for a 1 m window with plaster either side, and the 38 degree pitch keeps the ridge below twice the wall height so the hall reads long rather than tall.
